newsitem.title: USA: SEC sues CS First Boston over Orange County bonds.
newsitem.headline: SEC sues CS First Boston over Orange County bonds.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday it sued CS First Boston Corp and two of its former investment bankers for fraud in the offer and sale of Orange County, Calif., bonds.
The SEC said the lawsuit was the commission's third enforcement action in its continuing investigation of the Orange County bankruptcy, the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.
CS First Boston is a unit of CS Holding.
SEC filed its complaint in U.S. District Court for the Central District of California in Santa Ana, Calif.
In its complaint, the SEC alleged fraud in the offer and sale of $110 million of Series B pension obligation bonds issued by Orange County in September 1994.

The SEC said it is seeking permanent injunctions and unspecified civil penalties against the firm, a broker-dealer headquartered in New York, and the former investment bankers, identified as Jerry Nowlin and Douglas Montague.

The complaint alleged that, while participating in drafting and preparing of the county's bond offering documents, CS First Boston and the two bankers "knew, or were reckless in not knowing, significant negative information about the county (investment) pools that was misrepresented in or omitted from the official statement."
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
